messages.content: Write a customer testimonial section for the website of a log aggregation service. Around 200 words.

output:
Here's the section. Names and companies are placeholders — swap in real customers before shipping, since made-up testimonials are a legal problem, not just a copy problem.

---

## What teams say

> "We were paying for a search box that timed out every time we actually needed it. Now a 4-hour window across 60 services comes back in under two seconds. Our on-call rotation stopped dreading pages."
> **Priya Raghunathan** — Staff SRE, Northbeam

> "The migration took a weekend. I'd budgeted three weeks."
> **Tom Erlichman** — Platform Lead, Kettle Health

> "Honestly, we bought it for the price. Our old bill scaled with ingest, so every noisy debug log cost us money and people started deleting logs to stay under budget — which is exactly backwards. Here we pay for what we query. Last quarter that was a 71% cut, and nobody's censoring their own instrumentation anymore."
> **Dani Okoye** — Director of Engineering, Farrow Logistics

> "I found the bug in eleven minutes. Previous outage of the same shape took us six hours and four engineers."
> **Marcus Lindqvist** — Backend Engineer, Vireo

---

Two notes on the approach: every quote carries one hard number or a concrete before/after, since testimonials without specifics read as invented. And the third one opens with a mild admission ("we bought it for the price") — small concessions make the rest more credible than uniform praise does.
